By chance we came to Propoganda twice during our three-day visit to Saigon. We went on our first evening on the recommendation of friends who had been when they visited the city a few months ago. The next day we went on a tour which included lunch which happened to be at the same restaurant. 

On the first occasion I made a poor choice. The roast chicken with broken rice was OK but nothing special. It was not very different from roast chicken you could get anywhere in the UK, Our starter of spring rolls was much better, as was my cheesecake dessert, My wife made a much better choice She had pork meatballs, grilled pork and salad. She is still enthusing about her frozen banana with peanut butter and crushed peanuts.

On our second visit we given a set menu decided by the tour organisers and it was excellent. 

The decor is striking. Staff we helpful and spoke good English.

We would certainly go back on a future visit to the city

Amazing Food with Great Value and Vibe
Jan 2025 • Family
We happened to walk past this place whilst looking for a dinner location. It was very busy but we managed to get a table. We were told 30 min for food, but it didn't arrive after 1 hour and so we left. Apparently they had a gas issue in the kitchen. They were super apologetic and wanted to make amends so we booked same table for following night. When we returned we had an amazing experience. Food turned up after 20 min. They had good wine by the glass options from France and reds from Australia. Prices reasonable and menu a modern take on Vietnamese food. We ordered slow cooked beef, fried fish, noodle salad and I had homemade tofu and bean salad with endamame. The tofu was amazing and the dressing on the salad so delicious. Everyone was super happy with their main dishes and the fried and fresh spring rolls we ordered a entrees were really nice as well. We ordered the signature mango sticky rice and one serve of homemade ice cream for dessert to share and both were really great. The lady who normally organises the group functions was super helpful resolving our bill the first night and took personal care of us the 2nd night. I would highly recommend this restaurant for the food and the vibe is nice inside and out.

Cute, Eclectic Bistro in Heart of Ho Chi Minh City
Oct 2018 • Friends
We picked this restaurant off a guidebook map for its proximity to Notre Dame Cathedral. It’s tucked in among other restaurants on a bustling little street and was a little hard for us to find (our fault, not theirs). When we stopped to ask a local on the street for directions, she gushed about Propaganda Bistro. A hearty endorsement!

We arrived at 5pm for an early dinner and were given a table immediately. But by the time we left it was packed!

Communist propaganda-style murals covered the walls and was echoed on napkins, coasters and pillows adorning the long bench-like seats at the tables (you can even purchase bags, aprons and other store swag on premises). As night fell, the wall lamps were dimmed and waiters added tiny lit oil lamps to the tables to heighten the evening ambience. 

We were charmed and we hadn’t yet tasted the food, which was amazing! My friends and I all ordered the tri-colored rice (white rice, brown rice and another crunchy puffed rice we couldn’t identify). The texture was unliked anything we’d ever had in a rice dish - a perfect blend of soft and crisp. The dish was loaded with corn kernels, peas and other small vegetables, along with an abundance of seafood. It came with a small dish of sauce containing a single hot pepper. Don’t skip the sauce, even if they warn you about the pepper’s spiciness. The sauce itself was salty and savory, not hot (I just left the pepper in the dish after I poured out the sauce).

All in all a great experience! If we’re ever in HCMC again, we’ll definitely return here! It’s one not to be missed.

Hi Charles L,

We absolutely love our charming designs and colorful wall murals, commissioned especially for us by special local Vietnamese artists, however, we appreciate and understand that individuals are entitled to their own visual perspective and opinions, as you’ve kindly stated and shared.

A paradise for foodies !
Jan 2017 • Family
“Moi ngay ta chon mot mon an” reads below Propaganda’s large wall mural. It translates to “Every day we chose a new dish,” a play on a song lyric by Trinh Cong Son that goes something like “Every Day I Choose a New Joy.”

It underscores the Saigon bistro’s passion to continuously innovate and experiment.

The meaning of “bistro” is a place that packs a lot of value for its low price, a kinetic eatery with chatting waiters, chatting customers and groovy music jamming overhead.

Propaganda takes this to heart, with a unique playlist of funky tunes, a lively atmosphere and an off-the-beaten-track dining experience that’s been surprising locals and foreigners alike since the bistro’s inception.

A delicious and vibrant oasis
Oct 2016 • Family
Overlooking a small park adjacent the red-bricked Notre Dame cathedral lies the Propaganda bistro. The glass door opens and a fresh waft of conditioned air brings welcome respite from the humidity of Saigon.
With it's vibrant pop-art murals, white-washed brick and red mosaic tiled floors, the bistro is a delicious little oasis of fused old and new-world Vietnamese cuisine.
The crispy chicken and broken rice dish was delicious as was the prawn with broken rice dishes. The Vietnamese coffee was also delicious, served hot with a tin drip filter. Don't forget to stir as there is condensed milk at the bottom of the cup.
If your electronic devices are running low on power, there are power sockets at the base of the cushioned benches lining the side of the long mural wall; don't forget to bring your adapters.
This place is full of foreigners, so if you want to eat what the locals are eating, look outside of the district. If you want to eat delicious food in a comfortable restaurant with great service, then this is the place for you.

Jul 2015 • Family
While most people can agree that there's delicious Vietnamese food all around HCMC - from street stalls to upscale restaurants, the quality of food at Propaganda rests comfortably in the middle.

Traditional favorites served in larger portions in a very comfortable, social setting. There's good music and always a crowd. Service has always been very friendly. 

I particularly enjoy their not-so-traditional rice paper rolls. They're more akin to sushi rolls, and I highly recommend the chicken, avocado, brown rice rolls. Another unassuming favorite is the Grilled Eggplant. It's only 60k, and it's very flavorful, healthy and a wonderful side dish.

I also really enjoy their Bun Thit Nuong (grilled Pork w/ rice noodles) because they include a lot of fresh salad in this dish. 

For me, Propaganda is my go-to spot when I'm showing out-of-town guests around Vietnam. It's a very nice, easy way to introduce them to Vietnamese cuisine (before venturing into braver territory). They also have fantastic delivery, and I can trust that my food is clean.

Lonely Planet and Trip Advisor to the rescue! :-)

After reading about Propaganda and (and the numerous great reviews) we decided this was the place -- and loved it! Prices here are obviously more than you'll pay for street food, but the variety and quality of food here is top notch, and would cost twice as much in a similar restaurant in most other countries.

We had the spicy seafood soup with rice noodles and the pink pomelo and crab salad, topped off with sweet sticky rice with fresh mango and coconut sauce. The soup was heavenly, with just the right amount of heat for us, and the salad refreshing and different. And I'm just a sucker for a good sticky rice dessert......

The staff are super friendly and very professional, with an overall atmosphere that could make you feel like you were somehow transplanted to a trendy restaurant in any number of major cities around the globe (meaning all the best positives.....).

Very highly recommended. Don't wait until your last day in Saigon like we did though -- you'll want to go back again at some point.

But then it was so bad a few more times that we gave up sitting in Propaganda. The manager was very very nice and always tried to remedy anything that wasn't done properly, but ultimately there's only so much that can be done if the waiters are not good at their jobs. 

It got to the point where we wanted to eat Propaganda's food, but we couldnt deal with the potential frustration of the wait staff and we figured out that you can sit in Au Parc and still order from the Propaganda menu, so we just did that. Considering we'd walked what seemed like the whole length of HCMC, We felt extremely lucky to have stumbled on this restaurant, as we wilted in the hot and humid April weather. The food was absolutely the best Vietnamese food we've ever eaten and the ambience hit the spot perfectly. 

We wanted a relaxing, enjoyable evening meal accompanied by decent wine since we were only on a short break to HCM. A big plus for us was the outdoor seating so we could watch the world go by as we ate. We ordered fresh duck and betel leaf spring rolls, a tri-coloured rice seafood dish and a tofu noodle plate. The portions were generous, the flavours very clean and the food was definitely extremely fresh. Yes, we waited for our dishes to be served, but this made a nice change from the often hurried service, (and potentially dubiously microwaved food) often found in some Asian restaurants. We saw this as a sign of the kitchen making the meals to order, rather than lazy, indifferent service.

There was a good mixture of locals and expats, with fewer tourists than I would have expected. I think this would be a very top-end eating place for locals but I was still pleased I wasn't having a totally fake experience in a sanitised setting for tourists only.

Cindy, the Manager, was welcoming and supportive of her staff, a few of whom do not speak English fluently, but who nevertheless try their best. As a previous reviewer mentioned, if you're worried about not being understood, seek her out as she seems to be running the place and can step in if you need!

We also revisited the restaurant on our last night and weren't disappointed. Try the Pomelo juice or the lime sodas if you want non alcoholic options, and they have a good wine list which works well with the Vietnamese food. The duck curry was exceptional (think duck confit in fragrant coconut curry) and the fried spring rolls (crab and prawn / tofu) were first class.

Finally, when the bill came, it was not expensive (although it is special enough for a special occasion too). Our only regret is we don't live locally and it'll be a while before we can get back to eat the dishes we haven't yet tried
